text:
Owen Tippett is a big, fast shooter having a small season. Two goals and three points in 14 games is not what a player with 96th-percentile shot speed and 98th-percentile top speed is supposed to produce, and the trade rumour sites have noticed: his name has been linked to Seattle and Chicago in the last two weeks.

The finishing will probably come back. He's shooting 5.9% against a normal range of roughly 10 to 15%, and his 2.8 expected goals (the quality of his chances) say he's been about a goal unlucky. The bigger worry is everything around him. The Flyers have had only 38% of the expected goals at five on five with him on the ice since he came back from injury, and his minutes are down. Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking explains the style: 60% of his shots come off the rush, and he carries the puck in on 54% of his entries. He scored on the power play in Calgary on Saturday. If Philadelphia lets him run in transition, our range still has him finishing around 21 goals.
